prompt: In this essay I will explain how a discrete GPU is driven by two cooperating pieces of software: the kernel-mode driver, which owns the hardware, manages memory, schedules work onto engines and recovers from faults, and the user-mode runtime, which compiles kernels, allocates buffers and submits command streams. On Linux, Intel's Arc cards can be driven by either the older i915 driver or the newer xe driver, and the choice changes how work is submitted, how host memory is mapped for device access, how copies are routed between the compute and blitter engines, and how long-running compute jobs are policed. For a mixture-of-experts language model that keeps only half of its routed experts in video memory, every generated token forces the runtime to synchronize, read routing decisions back, and move expert weights across PCIe before the next layer can proceed.
